title: More options for DoseGuard
question: A fresh hand: the roll assigned the Fridge Reminder Card. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: Fridge Reminder Card
options.lineage: the clinic reminder card stuck on the fridge with today's times written in
options.thesis: Today is one calm card of time slots; the due slot carries a red pen box, finished slots get a clear tick.
options.viewport: White page, light-blue top bar; Today is one large card of ruled time rows, the due row boxed in red with Get my dose beside it.
options.risk: Can look plain if the tick and box states are drawn timidly.

raised.raise: Only the due slot is shown at full strength; every other slot steps back.
The dose steps show a tab rail with how far along you are and how much is left.
STOP and Skip this dose sit apart with empty space, never next to everyday buttons.
Time always reads one way, top to bottom, on every screen.

options.label: Pharmacy Prescription Label
options.lineage: printed pharmacy labels and red auxiliary warning stickers
options.thesis: Every dose reads like its pharmacy label: name, amount, time, with a red sticker only when action is needed.
options.viewport: Light-blue band header; the due dose shown as a large label with a red TAKE NOW sticker and one big button.
options.risk: Familiar health-app territory; the label idea is what many pharmacy apps already echo.

options.label: Paper Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: 1960s airline ticket wallets and carbon coupons
options.thesis: Each dose step is a coupon you tear off in order; used steps get stamped, nothing disappears.
options.viewport: Today shows the current dose as a ticket with stub coupons for each step; stamps mark done steps.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: stamped, never-erased states are perfect for taken-or-not clarity; loses some identification with a medicine setting.
options.risk: Travel flavour could distract if the ticket shape gets ornate.

options.label: Station Departure Board
options.thesis: Doses as departures in fixed rows; a change flips into place and the due row lights.
options.viewport: Today is a light departure board of dose rows ordered by time, the due row lit with Get my dose.
options.case: Fuses on clarity (time-ordered, held state) but its native black board fights the pinned light theme.
options.risk: Flip animations can feel busy for anxious users.

options.label: Factory Records Catalog
options.thesis: Colour codes instead of words on matte black.
options.viewport: A black field with a white line plot.
options.risk: Codes instead of words fail patients.
options.kept: Only the active item is shown at full strength.

options.label: Acetate Manual Tabs
options.thesis: Acetate leaves over coloured divider boards.
options.viewport: An open manual with a tab rail.
options.kept: A tab rail shows progress and what remains.

options.label: Dark Developer Console
options.risk: Dark tooling feel contradicts the light, calm brief.
options.kept: Dangerous actions sit apart with empty space.

options.label: Dance Notation Score
options.kept: Time always reads in one consistent direction.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean medication app like Apple Health: white rows, blue accent, red for alerts.
canonCard.viewport: A list of today's medicines with times and a Take button on the due one.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every medication app by design.
